cards.name: Minus 1.0
cards.summary: Darkens the whole image by 1 stop of exposure (values decoded from the .eap file: Exposure -1.00, Offset 0.00, Gamma Correction 1.00). On the test photo mean luminance goes from 103 to 77 (about x0.74); the 5th, 50th and 95th percentile luminance move from 50, 93, 181 to 37, 69, 136; no pixel reaches 250 or drops to 5, so nothing clips on this photo. Colours keep their hue (mean RGB 128/98/63 becomes 96/73/46) and the contrast between tones scales with the brightness: the picture simply looks one stop darker.
use_for: rescue an overexposed or washed-out photo
quick one-click darkening for a slightly bright photo
non-destructive darkening on an adjustment layer, masked to a region (sky, window light, vignette)
avoid: photos that are already dark: shadows block up
recovering blown-out highlights: exposure scales them down but cannot bring back clipped detail
fine control of highlights only: use Shadows/Highlights or Curves instead
cards.applies_to: a colour or grey image layer: as an adjustment layer (Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Exposure) it affects every layer below it (clip it to one layer to limit it); Image > Adjustments > Exposure applies it destructively to the selected pixel layer. Exposure was designed for 32-bit HDR images, but PGD applied it to an 8-bit RGB photo and it worked.
cards.how_to_apply: Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Exposure..., then in the Properties panel choose 'Minus 1.0' from the Preset menu (Photoshop lists the shipped presets by file name), or use Load Preset... and pick <Photoshop 2026 install folder>/Presets/Exposure/Minus 1.0.eap. Script: the Action Manager event 'exposure' with 'using' set to that .eap file, which is how PGD applied it on a scratch document (read-back of presetKind and using confirmed).
cards.notes: Values read from the .eap file (14 bytes: version 1, then three big-endian 32-bit floats: exposure, offset, gamma). Luminance figures are measured on PGD's thumbnail (test photo, result on top, untouched original below; Rec. 601 luminance; histogram change reported by the harvest: 108944). The thumbnail is a script application of the preset to the 8-bit RGB test photo.
